name: Chicken Bacon Ranch Burrito
writer_notes: TIKTOK source: macros rebuilt from ingredients against the food DB, not the caption. Stage 1 built this, numbers are ours.
CAP: rice cut from 100 g to 40 g cooked per burrito (14.3 g dry x 14 = 200 g dry). Do not restore the source rice load or it blows the 400 cal cap.
TURKEY BACON BID TRAP: ingredients.json Turkey Bacon.bid = bacon (pork by the lb). Needs turkey-bacon bid before costing or it prices as pork. Flagged in report.
Fat Free Cottage Cheese has no bid/packaging in ingredients.json (stub row): not cost-tracked. Flagged.
Bacon is the differentiator from ranch-chicken-burrito (T13). No direct bowl cousin.
intro_html: Under 400 calories, a full 4 ounces of chicken, and {{protein}} grams of protein, all wrapped in a tortilla that carries 18 grams of fiber for about 5 grams of net carb. That is the whole trick here. Bacon, ranch, and cheese usually means a calorie bomb, so we did the math instead of guessing. The ranch is a blended cottage cheese and Greek yogurt sauce, the bacon is turkey bacon crisped and crumbled, and the rice is measured, not dumped. It tastes like the indulgent one and eats like the disciplined one.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1582 g)
Fat Free Cottage Cheese (Great Value): 3 cups (700 g)
Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 1 chile, minced (7 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb: ~$7.78. Buy 4 lbs: $8.92.
Fat Free Cottage Cheese, 3 cups: ~$2.81. Buy 2 24oz tubs: $5.46.
Ranch Seasoning Mix, 4 tbsp: ~$0.45. Buy 1 (covers this batch).
Pantry seasonings (chipotle in adobo): ~$0.05. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $29.31 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.09 per burrito. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $43.05 across 14 servings, roughly $3.08 per burrito. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.14 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $49.19. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: That is about ${{cost_ps}} a burrito (at everyday cost) versus $10 or more for a fast-casual chicken burrito. Catch the breast on sale and it drops from there.
shop_smart: Buy the chicken on sale and freeze it. When breast drops in price, grab a big pack and split it into 3.5 pound bags. One sale trip covers a month of these.
One packet of ranch seasoning does the heavy lifting. A single 1 ounce packet flavors the whole batch of sauce, so you are not buying a bottle of dressing you will forget in the door of the fridge.
Turkey bacon stretches further than you think. A 12 ounce pack crisps down and crumbles across all 14 burritos. You want the crumble spread thin for the flavor, not stacked in strips.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook 1 cup of dry rice per the package and set it aside to cool.
Cube the chicken breast and cook it in a dry or lightly sprayed skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Cook the turkey bacon until crisp, then chop it into a fine crumble.
Make the ranch sauce: blend the fat free cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, ranch seasoning mix, and the minced chipotle in adobo until smooth.
Fold the ranch sauce and the reduced fat mozzarella into the warm chicken so the cheese melts in.
Stir in the rice, then the turkey bacon crumble. Finish with the sliced green onions and the lime juice.
Warm the tortillas so they roll without cracking, then fill and wrap each one.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down in Step 1. Divide that total food weight by 14 and scoop the same amount into each tortilla before you roll. Every burrito lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb (1582 g)
Fat Free Cottage Cheese, 3 cups (700 g)
Chipotle in Adobo, 1 chile, minced (7 g)
steps: Cook 1 cup dry rice per the package and cool.
Cube and cook the chicken breast until it reaches 165F.
Crisp the turkey bacon and chop into a crumble.
Blend the fat free cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, ranch seasoning, and chipotle into a smooth sauce.
Fold the sauce and mozzarella into the warm chicken, then stir in the rice, bacon, green onions, and lime juice.
Fill the warmed tortillas, weigh the batch, and divide into 14 equal burritos.
